tip: Não tem de quê is a set reply to obrigado (thanks). The words are fixed, so you do not change them.
To say how many are in a group, use ser plus a number: somos cinco = there are five of us.
têm with a circumflex is the vocês/eles form of ter. The singular tem has no accent.
tudo bom is a casual greeting, like how are you. You can also answer with tudo bom.
elas is they for an all-female group. Use eles if even one man is included.
descansa is the informal command. For -ar verbs the você command matches the ele form: descansa.
pela is por plus a, meaning through or via: pela internet = online.
algum means any or some and agrees with its noun: algum esporte, alguma ideia.
precisar plus an infinitive takes no preposition: preciso trocar. Before a noun you add de.
do is the contraction of de plus o, so longe do trabalho means far from work.
Language names stay lowercase in Portuguese: português and inglês are never capitalized.
devagar means slowly and is already an adverb, so it never takes the -mente ending.
nas is em plus as (in or on the, feminine plural): nas redes sociais.
fazer falta means to be missed: ele faz falta = the team misses him. Literally it means to make lack.
conhecer is to meet someone for the first time or to know a person, not to know a fact.
Portuguese has no apostrophe-s. Show possession with de: os textos dos alunos = the students' texts.
irmãos is masculine plural but can mean siblings of mixed gender, not only brothers.
dizer is irregular: eu digo, ele diz. Here diz means says.
desde marks a starting point in time, meaning since: desde a infância = since childhood.
como vão as coisas uses vão (they go) to ask how things are going.
carregar means both to charge a device and to carry: carrego o celular = I charge my phone.
tocar is to play an instrument. For sports and games use jogar instead.
passar roupa means to iron clothes, literally to pass clothes.
consertar means to fix or repair: ele conserta computadores. Do not confuse it with concerto, a concert.
à is the contraction of a plus a. à noite means at night.
pedir means to order or ask for and is irregular: eu peço, vocês pedem.
gastar com means to spend on. Use com, not em: gastamos com transporte.
An adjective plus demais means too or excessively: caro demais = too expensive.
o dia inteiro means all day long, literally the whole day.
